PullRequest.Title: Refine chat session indicators and add topology telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #332799 and #333253.

## State indicator feedback

- Removes the outer green frame while a request is running; the existing chat input progress border remains unchanged.
- Uses a green dotted one-stroke frame for an idle completion that has not been visited.
- Keeps the red dashed needs-input frame.
- Treats retained DOM focus as visited only while the owning window is focused, and recomputes on window focus/blur.
- Preserves a synchronous request-start edge when an accumulated add/complete batch is delivered after the model is already idle.
- Uses the same pending-aware idle rule as window notifications, including canceled/error-stranded queues.
- Relies on the effective `.monaco-reduce-motion` state instead of overriding it with a local OS media query.
- Clarifies the experimental setting description to match the states it now indicates.

## Chat Editor topology telemetry

Adds the count-only `chat.editorTopology` event after main-editor restoration and on coalesced topology changes involving Chat Editors:

- `openChatEditorCount`
- `visibleChatEditorCount`
- `chatEditorGroupCount`
- `visibleEditorCount`
- `editorGroupCount`

The event excludes dedicated Agents windows, is scoped to the main editor part, suppresses identical snapshots, and collects no session IDs, resources, titles, prompts, or content.

## Validation

- Targeted ESLint and telemetry classification checks
- Targeted stylelint
- `npm run compile-client`
- ChatWidget, ChatWindowNotifier, and ChatEditorTopologyTelemetry unit tests
- Staged-file hygiene
- Live Code OSS validation of running and unvisited visual states

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: An infinite CSS animation changed a large blurred box-shadow on a pseudo-element covering the entire chat widget while each request was in progress, forcing continuous rendering/paint work until completion.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Sustained CPU/GPU paint load and potential dropped frames while a chat request runs, especially for large chat editor surfaces or multiple simultaneously visible sessions.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: In-progress sessions no longer create or animate the full-widget pseudo-element; only static idle-unvisited and needs-input frames remain, eliminating the continuous large-area box-shadow repaint during long-running requests.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base CSS applies `animation: chat-session-working-glow 1.4s ease-in-out infinite` to the full-widget `.interactive-session.chat-state-in-progress::before` overlay. The keyframes animate `box-shadow` from spacing-size20 to spacing-size60, so every active chat request continuously repaints a large blurred region for the request lifetime. This PR deletes both the in-progress pseudo-element selector and the infinite box-shadow animation, while `ChatWidget.updateSessionStateIndicator` still transitions request state normally.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render chat request progress and unvisited-completion state in a chat editor/widget
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accumulated ChatViewModel changes synchronously call updateWorkingProgressBorder and updateSessionStateIndicator before the widget change handler continues. The added idle calculation, focus check, and class toggles are O(1) per delivered batch; CSS state then renders asynchronously. The PR removes the prior full-surface infinite box-shadow paint loop.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Delivered ChatViewModel event batches and number of visible chat widgets; the removed paint workload also scaled with request duration and widget area.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One accumulated event callback per widget batch; multiple visible chat widgets update independently. No queue or external concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. State is read directly from the model; accumulated model events coalesce synchronous add/complete handoffs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, O(1) model reads, DOM class mutations, and deleted infinite box-shadow animation are explicit in the changed hunks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Streaming batch frequency and the number/size of simultaneously visible chat widgets vary, but the newly added synchronous work is constant and dominated by existing list updates. The removed animation had duration proportional to request lifetime and surface area.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. State work remains bounded, and the rendering change removes a continuous large-area repaint mechanism; that fix was recorded separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Track chat model idle transitions and deliver completion/needs-input window notifications
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each live model is observed for request, needs-input, last-response, and pending-queue changes. A busy-to-idle transition schedules the existing 500 ms notification check; only a qualifying notification proceeds to OS focus/toast operations. The PR extracts the idle computation into a shared helper without increasing observer count or boundary cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Focus/notify a native window and show an OS toast through IHostService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one toast path per qualifying needs-input or coalesced busy-to-idle transition per model, subject to settings, focus checks, and dedupe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The notifier already performed the same host focus/toast operations and used the same idle observable logic inline; the diff only moves that logic to observeChatModelIsIdle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the chat response critical path after the existing delay; only notification delivery awaits the host calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live chat models and qualifying state transitions; no diff-introduced multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One tracker and one RunOnceScheduler per live model; repeated state changes replace/cancel the pending idle check. OS notification calls remain per qualifying session transition.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache. Observable dependencies suppress reevaluation until relevant model state changes, and RunOnceScheduler coalesces transient idle gaps. Notification dedupe remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after code shows a direct extraction of the existing derived idle computation, including the same pending-queue and error/cancellation rules.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously live chat models varies, but each model had an existing tracker and the helper reads constant-time fields/array length.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; boundary count, scheduling, lifecycle disposal, and per-model work are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collect main-editor Chat Editor topology telemetry after restoration and on editor/group changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initialization awaits main editor restoration asynchronously without blocking workbench progress. Each event burst schedules one snapshot after 100 ms; snapshot construction synchronously copies/scans all main-part groups and open editors, compares five counts, and calls telemetry only for a distinct topology entering, changing within, or leaving a Chat Editor state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the count-only `chat.editorTopology` usage event via ITelemetryService/publicLog2 (subject to telemetry buffering, level, and appender behavior).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial eligible event after restoration and at most one event per distinct count snapshot after 100 ms coalescing; identical snapshots and all steady no-Chat snapshots are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Chat Editor topology snapshot or telemetry boundary existed before this contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The publicLog2 call is made after the scheduled snapshot and does not await network completion; it is off editor restoration and navigation progress except for the small synchronous handoff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total open editors across main-part groups after coalescing, not raw editor event count; telemetry cardinality is distinct count snapshots while Chat Editors are present or on exit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single RunOnceScheduler serializes and coalesces events; there is at most one pending scan and no concurrent telemetry burst from this contribution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: previousSnapshot is a one-entry warm cache that suppresses identical snapshots. Cold startup performs one full scan; without a Chat Editor it sends nothing. Warm event bursts still scan all open main-part editors, but coalescing limits scans to 10/s and telemetry remains suppressed unless counts change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the O(open editors + groups) scan, one-snapshot retention, coalescing, and telemetry reachability; lower only for telemetry transport details because appenders are abstracted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Open-tab counts and editor-event burst rates vary; scans allocate arrays proportional to open editors, but realistic cardinality plus 100 ms coalescing does not establish user-visible latency or GC pressure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The contribution introduces bounded linear snapshot work and a telemetry boundary, but coalescing, constant-size retention, identical-snapshot suppression, and realistic editor cardinality do not support a concrete user-visible performance impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recompute chat visited state on widget focus, mouse interaction, and owning-window blur
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Focus or mouse-down clears an existing unvisited flag and performs one state/class update; window blur performs one update per live widget. These handlers are synchronous but contain only constant-time model/focus reads and class toggles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live chat widgets on a window blur, or direct interactions with one widget.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser events dispatch serially; each widget owns and disposes its three listeners with the widget Disposable store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The `_hasUnvisitedCompletion` flag acts as a guard: focus/mouse handlers return immediately once visited. There is no external cache or I/O.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener registration, guard, synchronous update path, and disposal ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of live widgets in a window varies, but blur is infrequent and widget count is normally small; no unbounded listener retention is introduced because ownership is registered.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; work is bounded and listeners are disposed with widget lifecycle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files and all diff pages. No actionable diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. The only concrete performance mechanism is a fix: removal of the full-widget infinite box-shadow animation, recorded against its introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
